title: Graduating Sherman: the Cruz family band and Max Melody Makers
summary: After graduating in 1933 he rehearsed a Mexican dance band for the Cruz family and then joined Max Rangel's Max Melody Makers in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Ok. Let's see. Are there any other things you'd like to say as far as being in California? You eventually -- 1935 was a big year for you. Something very important happened then. You were a young man about 22-23 years old, and a gentleman by the name of Lionel Hampton . . .
Oh yes, yes, yes. I'm gonna start from the time I graduated at Sherman in 1933.

Well in, during the year 1933, there used to be a Mexican band out of Santa An a. And the family that, that had the band in the, in, in the, in the dance business, the dance-hall business -- they had the band, and they asked me, "You're a graduate, Russell; why don't you come and live with us and rehearse our band?" So I did. When I graduated, I went right straight to be with the Cruzes. His name was Jim Cruz, Big Jim Cruz. And a, was a nice family, and I rehearsed their bands, and we played dances. And then I was gettin' my recognition there, and, from there, I left the Cruzes to go into Los Angeles with the, with the band called Max Melody Makers. And, from there, I . . .
Who was the leader of that band, of Max Melody Makers? Do you recall?
The leader of Max Melody . . . was -- his name was Max Rangel.
